# Research Evidence Dossier: Daily Digest Issue #106

**Research Date Window**: November 21, 2026 – November 28, 2026 (`search_window`: 7 days)  
**Target Issue**: #106  
**Curatorial Focus**: Feminist visual culture, photography/photobooks, East Asian image archives, AI-native creative workflows, and archival opportunities.

---

### Candidate 1: Feminist Structure Signal
* **Proposed Title**: Käthe Kollwitz Museum Köln Opens *Hanna Nagel: Wiederentdeckung einer Pionierin feministischer Kunst*
* **Category**: Feminist Structure Signal
* **Source URL**: `https://www.kollwitz.de/`
* **Publication / Opening Date**: November 27, 2026 (Exhibition period: Nov 27, 2026 – Feb 20, 2027)
* **Institutional Context**: Käthe Kollwitz Museum Köln, in collaboration with Kunsthalle Mannheim.
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Features around 100 drawings and prints created during the 1920s and 1930s by German artist Hanna Nagel (1907–1975).
  * Nagel was a master student of Emil Orlik in Berlin.
  * Works directly critique patriarchal power structures, marriage, forced domesticity, motherhood, unemployment, and male dominance over women.
  * The show spans her early critical graphic sheets, self-portraits exploring motherhood, and her dark, mythological *Dunkle Blätter* (Dark Sheets) created in Rome.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Highlights an essential early 20th-century feminist printmaker whose graphic critique of women's physical and labor conditions provides historical grounding for feminist visual culture.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New. No prior mention in the past 7 issues.

### Candidate 2: Visual Culture Signal
* **Proposed Title**: George Eastman Museum Announces *GAG*: Reframing 21st-Century Photography and Video Through Visual Interruption
* **Category**: Visual Culture Signal
* **Source URL**: `https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/637375/gag/`
* **Publication Date**: November 23, 2026 (Exhibition period: Oct 2, 2026 – Apr 11, 2027)
* **Institutional Context**: George Eastman Museum, Rochester, NY (Curated by Phil Taylor, Associate Curator of Photography).
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Introduces "gag" as a critical framework for contemporary photography and moving image practice.
  * Traces the term from cinematic sight gags to queer ballroom culture, BDSM/kink, judicial gag orders, physical retching, and algorithmic feedback loops in social media.
  * Features works by Peggy Ahwesh, Lucas Blalock, Patty Chang, Talia Chetrit, Buck Ellison, and others.
  * Focuses on visual practices that disrupt seamless image consumption through slapstick, anxiety, and structural interruption.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Connects photographic history with internet subcultures, queer media vernaculars, and bodily performance, offering a fresh lens for image archaeology.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New. No prior mention in the past 7 issues.

### Candidate 3: China / East Asia Signal
* **Proposed Title**: Asia Art Archive Presents *Days We Inherit*: Revisiting 1990s Korean Contemporary Art Through Personal Memories and Archives
* **Category**: China / East Asia Signal
* **Source URL**: `https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/637841/days-we-inherit/`
* **Publication Date**: November 25, 2026 (Exhibition period: Dec 3, 2026 – Jan 16, 2027)
* **Institutional Context**: Asia Art Archive (AAA), Hong Kong (Curated by Hyejung Jang).
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Part of an 18-month pilot project supported by the Korea Arts Management Service to document Korean contemporary art from the 1980s and 1990s.
  * Features four artists: Ahn Kyuchul, Oh Inhwan (who experienced the 1990s firsthand), Noh Songhee, and Park Sunho (born in the 1990s, engaging via oral history and archives).
  * Each artist selects a single date of personal significance to transform subjective memory into shared historical archive.
  * Ahn Kyuchul revisits his 1991 conceptual work *Water from Afar II*, created during his time in Germany amid Korean political turmoil; Oh Inhwan revisits *Flower Arrangement for Men*.
  * Reverses AAA's 2024 archival exhibition methodology from *Another Day in Hong Kong*.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Exemplifies East Asian archival practices where contemporary artists directly intervene in image history, intergenerational memory, and media archaeology.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New. No prior mention in the past 7 issues.

### Candidate 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
* **Proposed Title**: Researchers Introduce VibeVideoAgent: Closing the Multimodal Perceptual Loop for Code-Driven Video Generation
* **Category**: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
* **Source URL**: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34237`
* **Publication Date**: November 25, 2026 (arXiv:2611.34237)
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Addresses code-driven generative video workflows where LLM coding agents write rendering scripts for motion, typography, data visualization, and synchronized audio.
  * Identifies the core workflow challenge: program execution errors do not capture perceptual flaws (e.g., overlapping text, off-camera rendering, out-of-sync audio).
  * Introduces VibeVideoAgent, a training-free framework that isolates short-lived multimodal inspection contexts from the primary coder, generating compact feedback ("Findings").
  * Operates across a unified multi-clock representation to evaluate preview drafts, verify multi-modal timing, and fix audio-visual alignment prior to full-resolution rendering.
  * Demonstrates substantial gains on 239 VibeVideoBench tasks, improving holistic audiovisual quality (L3) and rubric compliance (L2), with audio-sync score increasing by up to +0.56.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly impacts AI-native creative workflows by solving perceptual feedback and multi-modal alignment in program-driven video editing.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New. No prior mention in the past 7 issues.

### Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
* **Proposed Title**: ARCHAIVE Launches Open Call for 2027 Residencies: Exploring Generative AI, Media Archives, and Cultural Memory
* **Category**: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
* **Source URL**: `https://on-the-move.org/news/archaive-residency-ai-and-cultural-memory-2027-germany-italy-netherlands-portugal-spain-remote`
* **Publication Date**: November 2026 (Application Deadline: December 7, 2026)
* **Institutional Context**: Consortium of 5 European partners across Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Portugal, and Spain.
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Invites emerging and mid-career artists to engage with generative AI across six media art archives housed by European partner institutions.
  * Focuses on how generative AI acts as a critical tool to query, reconstruct, and question media archives and cultural memory—examining how algorithms read, complete, or distort historical records.
  * Provides a €5,000 artist fee, research resources, and access to partner archives.
  * Eligible for nationals or residents of Creative Europe countries.
* **Relevance to Muki**: An open call at the intersection of media archaeology, archive critique, and creative technology.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New. No prior mention in the past 7 issues.
